title: I participi irregolari
summary: The top irregular past participles you can't derive from the -ato/-uto/-ito rule

blocks.title: The rebels of the participio
blocks.body: Many of the most-used verbs **don't** follow -ato/-uto/-ito — they're irregular and just need memorizing. Most still use **avere**; only a few (like *venire* or *stare*) use essere.
blocks.callout: There's no *faciuto* or *dicito* — it's *fatto* and *detto*, full stop.

blocks.title: The 12 to know right away
blocks.body: These are the most common irregular participles — learn the list, the rest come with practice.

blocks.title: Listen to the most common ones

blocks.explain: *Vedere → visto* — irregular, learn it as a whole word.
*Fare → fatto* — one of the most-used irregular participles, period.

pairs.note: Same structure (avere + participle), but the ending has to be learned case by case.

blocks.prompt: Type 'I took the train' — passato prossimo.
blocks.explain: *Ho preso il treno* — preso is the irregular participle of prendere.
